tasks.short: Unload incoming mail containers onto handling equipment for transport to the sorting area.

steps.what: Check container stability, handling needs and available space.
Unload containers onto a trolley or other suitable handling equipment.

tasks.design: Keep unloading with trained staff using suitable handling equipment and approved instructions in {DOCS}. No software build is justified for the physical transfer itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires physical handling in a changing space. Software cannot lift containers.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability changes this task. Existing handling aids may improve ergonomics where suitable.
tasks.still_hard: Unstable loads, awkward parcels, restricted space and equipment suitability require local assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice an unstable container and change the handling method before anyone is hurt.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the person's week or decision rights from software alone.

reach.task: Receive deliveries and record visible damage.
reach.learn: Delivery reconciliation, custody records and safe handling procedures.

evidence.claim: Physical unloading remains manual without a separate handling-equipment investment; software automation is not a substitute.

assumptions: The company receives ordinary office mail and parcels rather than operating a distribution hub.
The scope excludes buying or redesigning physical handling equipment.
Time shares are estimates; no software time saving is assumed.
unknowns: Container weights, arrival volumes and available handling equipment.
Local handling restrictions and staff training.
Whether any deliveries can arrive directly at their destination.
research_questions: Would changing the delivery point remove an unloading transfer?
Would a handling-equipment assessment identify a worthwhile ergonomic improvement?

tasks.short: Check mail addresses, postage and physical condition, and resolve items that cannot be processed.

steps.what: Read the address and check that required delivery details are present.
Check weight, service and postage using the postage meter in {OTHER}.
Inspect the packaging, closure and visible damage.
Hold unsuitable items and send the sender a correction request.
Confirm corrected delivery details, service or packaging instructions.

tasks.design: Validate structured dispatch instructions in {WORKFLOW} before labels are produced, and configure the postage meter in {OTHER} with approved services and current rates. Keep physical inspection and placement on the scale with the clerk; use {WORKFLOW} and {EMAIL} for exception requests, with sender approval before changed dispatch instructions take effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Addresses arrive on physical items, dispatch requests vary, and postage settings are separate from sender details.
tasks.enabler_now: A small form, deterministic address checks and existing meter settings can prevent repeat checks for internally prepared mail. AI-assisted coding can shorten implementation without changing the underlying capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Address completeness does not prove deliverability. Handwritten mail, purchased stamps, unusual contents and damaged packaging still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently valid item is unsuitable for processing and obtain the sender's intended correction.

ambition.what: A pre-dispatch check for occasional internal senders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time finding missing details and chasing routine corrections. The role can recommend a suitable service within an agreed budget; destination changes remain with the sender.

reach.learn: Service restrictions, packaging requirements and dispatch records.

evidence.claim: Structured address checks, postage tables and template notifications can use deterministic rules; physical inspection remains necessary.
The remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Most checked items are outgoing office mail prepared internally.
Structured instructions replace address checking only for labels generated from those instructions; other items remain manually checked.
An existing postage meter supports service and rate configuration.
The consent range includes access review and any consultation required under national rules.
GDPR applies to address data; the EU AI Act applies where AI is used. This design requires no model.
unknowns: Share of mail with structured dispatch instructions.
Available meter settings, interfaces and rate-update arrangements.
Frequency of address errors, packaging faults and sender corrections.
Applicable national consultation requirements and local approval limits.
research_questions: Which checks can move into dispatch preparation and disappear from repeat handling?
Can approved service presets remove manual rate selection?
Does the proposed form reduce total sender and clerk time?
new_work: Maintain address rules and approved service presets.
Check failed notifications and unresolved holds.
Sample generated labels against their dispatch instructions.

tasks.short: Stop mail equipment, clear permitted jams safely and verify that operation can resume.

steps.what: Stop and isolate the equipment according to the approved procedure.
Inspect the accessible mail path and locate the obstruction.
Check the operating instructions for permitted recovery or maintenance escalation.
Remove accessible jammed mail, or leave equipment isolated for maintenance.
Check guards, authorise restart and test the cleared equipment.

tasks.design: Configure an equipment-specific index in {DOCS} that opens the approved recovery procedure and maintenance contact. Keep isolation, physical clearance and restart with authorised people; no generated repair advice or remote restart is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most time is spent inspecting and handling equipment. Instructions may also be difficult to find at the machine.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document links and search can shorten instruction lookup. No model or technical breakthrough is required.
tasks.still_hard: Equipment condition and safe access must be assessed locally. Some jams require a maintenance technician.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the obstruction exceeds operator training and stop the recovery attempt.
tasks.altitude: Instruction lookup becomes shorter, but physical work and restart authority stay with authorised staff. Nothing else changes in the person's decision rights.

reach.learn: Fault categorisation, maintenance escalation and equipment service records.

evidence.claim: An approved procedure index can reduce lookup effort; it cannot physically clear equipment or establish safe restart conditions.
Time shares, lookup savings and build ranges are estimates for a modest office mailroom.

assumptions: The site has mail-processing equipment with operator-clearable jams.
Approved operating instructions are available in or can be indexed through {DOCS}.
The clerk clears only jams permitted by training and equipment instructions.
The workflow is conditional: unresolved faults go to maintenance instead of restart.
unknowns: Equipment types, approved isolation procedures and operator permissions.
Whether staff currently consult instructions during jam recovery.
Whether instruction lookup is already immediate.
research_questions: Would a direct procedure link save enough time to justify maintaining it?
Do recurring jams indicate a feeding, consumables or maintenance problem that could remove the task?
new_work: Keep procedure links aligned with equipment and manual revisions.
Verify access to instructions at the point of use.

tasks.short: Sort mail into destination bins or sacks and attach identifying tags.

steps.what: Read the destination and decide the appropriate internal route or dispatch group.

loop.input: Address image for an item without a recognised routing code.
loop.output: Visible recipient and destination text, with uncertain fields marked.
loop.check: Require source-image traceability and an unambiguous match against the approved routing directory. The clerk confirms the destination before placement.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt per item. Missing, ambiguous or unmatched text goes to manual reading; never guess a recipient.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use exact routing-code matches first. Mixed printed and handwritten address text needs extraction; rules alone cannot read all remaining items.

steps.what: Place the item into the selected bin or sack.
Write a destination and collection identifier on the bin or sack tag.
Attach the identifying tag to the matching bin or sack.

tasks.design: Use a routing table in {WORKFLOW}, fed by a limited recipient-location extract from {HCM}, and match routing codes deterministically. For uncoded items, a bounded extraction loop proposes a destination for clerk confirmation; print reusable destination tags through a label printer in {OTHER}. Physical placement and tag attachment remain manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipient knowledge sits with experienced clerks, addresses vary, and physical sorting limits the value of software alone.
tasks.enabler_now: A small routing application and tag generator are straightforward to build. Bounded image extraction can assist with residual address text while leaving routing confirmation with the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: Outdated recipient locations, shared names, confidential addressees and wrong-bin placement remain difficult. Capture effort may outweigh reading savings at low volumes.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous recipients and recognise mail that needs restricted handling.

ambition.what: Temporary cover staff who need to sort mail without memorising internal routes.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time writing tags and recalling destinations, and more time resolving unclear items. The role can propose routing-directory corrections; employee-location changes remain with the authorised records owner.

reach.task: Route scanned correspondence to an authorised document collection.
reach.learn: Document classification, access restrictions and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: PostNL documents business-post scanning and form digitisation. This supports capture feasibility, not automated physical sorting.
Routing-code lookup and destination-tag generation can use deterministic code; address extraction needs a bounded fallback only where codes are absent.
Remaining-time percentages and build ranges are estimates; the digest provides no matching physical-sorting benchmark.

assumptions: The mailroom sorts office-scale volumes into a manageable set of routes.
Tags are currently written; reusable tags should be tried before adding a generator.
Extraction is limited to the visible address area, not confidential letter contents.
GDPR data minimisation, access and retention controls apply; EU AI Act obligations depend on the deployed use.
The access range includes any employee consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Mail volumes, destination counts and time spent identifying recipients.
Availability and accuracy of recipient-location data in {HCM}.
Share of items with usable routing codes or machine-readable addresses.
Current use of reusable tags and available capture equipment.
Required access approvals and national consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Can fixed labelled bins eliminate repeated tag preparation?
Does address capture plus review beat direct reading on representative items?
Can sender-applied routing codes remove enough extraction to avoid a model?
What routing errors occur when names or locations change?
new_work: Maintain routing mappings and recipient-location feeds.
Monitor destination errors and capture effort without individual productivity scoring.
Maintain extraction checks and address-image deletion settings.

role.altitude: Most of the week remains physical handling, inspection and sorting. Software can reduce address lookup, tag writing and exception administration; broader dispatch authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerk: delivery reconciliation and parcel dispatch preparation.
File clerk: controlled routing of scanned correspondence.
Facilities manager: evidence on recurring mail-equipment interruptions.
skills_to_grow: Structured dispatch preparation and service selection.
Safe equipment recovery within authorised procedures.
Exception analysis and testing of routing suggestions.
role.ambitious_version: Run a dependable mail-intake and dispatch service that occasional senders and cover staff can use, with clear routes, fewer avoidable holds and visible unresolved exceptions.

job.title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
